mainTopic: Is טומאה in public offerings הותרה or דחויה? This is shown through the תנאים dispute over when the ציץ is מרצה, and through how each side reads 'תמיד' in the פסוק.
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא which says that טומאה in public offerings 'was permitted' (הותרה). That wording seems to challenge רב ששת, who holds that public טומאה is only דחויה (overridden). The גמרא answers that this is a dispute among תנאים. רבי שמעון holds the ציץ is מרצה even when it is not on the כהן גדול's forehead. רבי יהודה holds it works only while it is worn. Their debate about the כהן גדול on יום הכיפורים shows that רבי שמעון holds טומאה דחויה בציבור, so רב ששת follows him. אביי then narrows the dispute: everyone agrees a broken ציץ does not work, and they argue only about an intact ציץ hanging on a peg. Each side learns its view from a different part of the same פסוק. For רבי שמעון, 'תמיד' means the ציץ always brings acceptance. For רבי יהודה, 'תמיד' means the כהן גדול must never take his mind off the ציץ. The amud ends with רבה בר רב הונא's rule that a person must regularly touch his תפילין, learned by a קל וחומר from the ציץ. The details of that קל וחומר come on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא's conclusion challenges רב ששת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that the ציץ only atones for טומאה that was 'permitted' in public. This challenges רב ששת, who holds that טומאה is only 'overridden' (דחויה) in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the ציץ only bears the sin of impurity, which was permitted out of its general rule in public cases. This is difficult for רב ששת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא and points out that its wording contradicts רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls טומאה in public 'הותרה', meaning fully permitted. רב ששת holds that public טומאה is only דחויה, meaning pushed aside but still not ideal. If the ברייתא says 'permitted', it seems to support רב נחמן and not רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: The sin of impurity (an offering or service that became impure)
From its general rule (as an exception to the usual ban)

steps.confusionAlert: The first line is not a new statement. It is the end of a ברייתא that began on the previous amud. The challenge comes only with 'וקשיא לרב ששת'.

phrases.english: Apparently, it bears only
the sin of impurity
which was permitted out of its general rule in public cases.
phrases.notes: End of the ברייתא quoted on the previous amud.

phrases.english: And this is difficult for Rav Sheshet!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the ברייתא quoted earlier and turns it into a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's view that טומאה דחויה בציבור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly says 'הותרה', meaning permitted, which contradicts 'דחויה'.

steps.title: It is a dispute of תנאים: רבי שמעון's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this question is a תנאים dispute. It brings a ברייתא where רבי שמעון says the ציץ is מרצה whether or not it is on the forehead.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute of תנאים. As it was taught: The ציץ is מרצה whether it is on his forehead or not on his forehead. These are the words of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת by saying the issue is argued among תנאים. It begins quoting the ברייתא that shows this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת does not need to agree with every ברייתא. He can side with one תנא against another. Here רבי שמעון's opinion is introduced first: the ציץ's power to bring acceptance does not depend on its being worn.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among Tannaim
The golden frontplate worn by the כהן גדול
Brings acceptance (makes an impure offering acceptable)

phrases.english: It is a dispute of Tannaim.
As it was taught in a baraita: The frontplate,
whether it is on his forehead
or whether it is not on his forehead —
it effects acceptance; these are the words of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Tannaitic dispute (the opposing ברייתא follows a different תנא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's word 'הותרה' is binding on everyone, so רב ששת is refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The matter is argued by תנאים, and רב ששת can follow רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only while it is on his forehead
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the ציץ is מרצה only while it is actually on the כהן גדול's forehead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: While it is still on his forehead, it is מרצה. If it is no longer on his forehead, it is not מרצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יהודה's opposing opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the ציץ works only when it is physically worn. This sets up the debate that follows.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
As long as it is on his forehead — it effects acceptance.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עוֹדֵהוּ עַל מִצְחוֹ — אֵינוֹ מְרַצֶּה.
phrases.english: If it is no longer on his forehead — it does not effect acceptance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ציץ is מרצה only while it is worn on the forehead.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's proof from יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון challenges רבי יהודה from the כהן גדול on יום הכיפורים. He is not wearing the ציץ then, yet it still brings acceptance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said to him: The כהן גדול on יום הכיפורים will prove it. The ציץ is not on his forehead, and still it is מרצה!
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, רבי שמעון attacks רבי יהודה's view with a counter-example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכיפורים the כהן גדול performs the special inner services in four white linen garments, without the ציץ. רבי שמעון assumes the ציץ still covers any impure offerings during those services. So the ציץ must work even when it is not being worn.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said to him:
The High Priest on Yom Kippur will prove it,
for it is not on his forehead, and yet it effects acceptance!
phrases.notes: During the special יום הכיפורים services he wears only the four white garments, with no ציץ.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's rule that the ציץ works only when worn
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On יום הכיפורים the ציץ is not worn, yet it is assumed to atone, which contradicts רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: יום הכיפורים needs no ציץ
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that יום הכיפורים is no proof. On that day טומאה is permitted for public offerings, so the ציץ is not needed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: Leave aside the כהן גדול on יום הכיפורים. For him, טומאה was permitted in public cases.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה deflects רבי שמעון's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יום הכיפורים offerings are public offerings. רבי יהודה holds טומאה הותרה בציבור, so impurity there is fully allowed. No atonement from the ציץ is needed, and the case proves nothing about the ציץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave aside (that case is no proof)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him:
Leave aside the High Priest on Yom Kippur,
for impurity was permitted for him in public cases.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (no ציץ is needed there)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: On יום הכיפורים the ציץ atones even though it is not worn.
steps.terutzMaskana: On יום הכיפורים טומאה is permitted for public offerings, so the ציץ plays no role.

steps.title: רבי שמעון holds impurity is only overridden
steps.stepSummary: From this exchange the גמרא infers that רבי שמעון holds טומאה דחויה בציבור. That is רב ששת's view, so רב ששת has a תנא to rely on.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn by inference that רבי שמעון holds that טומאה is only overridden (דחויה) in public cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion that rescues רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון insisted that the ציץ is needed on יום הכיפורים. That only makes sense if public impurity still carries a flaw that needs atonement, which is דחויה. So רב ששת follows רבי שמעון, and the earlier ברייתא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה = טומאה הותרה בציבור (like רב נחמן). רבי שמעון = טומאה דחויה בציבור (like רב ששת). So the ברייתא's word 'הותרה' is no refutation of רב ששת.

phrases.english: Learn by inference that Rabbi Shimon holds
that impurity is overridden in public cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא's exchange that completes the answer to step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הותרה/דחויה question is a תנאים dispute. רב ששת follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties an אמוראים dispute to a תנאים dispute, so both רב ששת and רב נחמן stand on solid ground.

steps.title: אביי: broken frontplate never works; dispute is about a peg
steps.stepSummary: אביי narrows the dispute. A broken ציץ does not work according to everyone. רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה only argue about an intact ציץ hanging on a peg.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Where the ציץ broke, everyone agrees it is not מרצה. Where they argue is when it is hanging on a peg.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new discussion that defines the exact case of the רבי שמעון/רבי יהודה dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think רבי שמעון means the ציץ works no matter what, even when broken. אביי limits this. The ציץ must still exist whole. The only question is whether it must be worn or just exist intact, for example hanging on a peg.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Where the frontplate broke,
everyone agrees
that it does not effect acceptance.
Where they disagree is when it is hanging on a peg,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בְּנִשְׁבַּר הַצִּיץ דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from using the ברייתא to analyzing its exact case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A broken ציץ is never מרצה. The dispute is only about an intact ציץ that is not being worn, such as one hanging on a peg.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's source from the verse
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins to explain רבי יהודה's source: the פסוק links 'on the forehead' with 'and he shall bear' the sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds: 'On the forehead ... and he shall bear.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts to give the פסוק behind רבי יהודה's view. The explanation continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (שמות כח:לח) says the ציץ will be 'על מצח אהרן ונשא אהרן'. רבי יהודה reads the two parts together. The ציץ bears the sin only while it is on the forehead.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall bear (the sin, i.e. bring atonement)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds:
"On the forehead ... and he shall bear" (Exodus 28:38),
phrases.notes: The verse links wearing the ציץ with its atoning power.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's statement by giving רבי יהודה's scriptural basis.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה derives from 'על מצח ... ונשא' that the ציץ atones only while worn.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's source: 'always for acceptance'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that רבי שמעון learns his view from the end of the פסוק: 'תמיד לרצון לפני ה׳.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון holds: 'always for acceptance before ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: Step 8 showed that רבי יהודה focuses on 'on the forehead.' Now the גמרא gives רבי שמעון's source, which is a different part of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון links the word 'תמיד' (always) to 'לרצון' (for acceptance). In his reading, the ציץ always brings acceptance, so it does not have to be on the forehead to work. The next step will prove why 'תמיד' must be read this way.

keyTerms.meaning: For acceptance (so that the offerings are accepted)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon holds
"Always, for acceptance before the Lord."
phrases.notes: שמות כח:לח, the end of the פסוק about the ציץ

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 8. Step 8 gave רבי יהודה's source, and this step gives רבי שמעון's source from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון derives from 'תמיד לרצון' that the ציץ always brings acceptance.

steps.title: Proving that 'always' cannot mean 'always on the forehead'
steps.stepSummary: The ציץ cannot physically stay on the forehead all the time, because the כהן גדול must go to the bathroom and must sleep. So 'תמיד' must mean that the ציץ always brings acceptance.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'always' mean? If you say it means always on his forehead, is that even possible? Doesn't he need to go to the bathroom? Doesn't he need to sleep? Rather, it means it always brings acceptance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רבי שמעון's reading. It does this by showing that the other possible reading cannot work in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'תמיד' needs a meaning that fits reality. A כהן גדול cannot wear the ציץ (which has ה׳'s name on it) in the bathroom, and he does not sleep in it. So 'always on the forehead' is impossible, and the word must describe the ציץ's power: it always brings acceptance, even when it is not being worn.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a reading the גמרא will reject)
Can you find such a case? (is that even possible?)
Brings acceptance / makes the offering acceptable

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'תמיד מרצה' means the ציץ works no matter what. Step 7 already taught that a broken ציץ does not work for anyone. This argument is only about an intact ציץ that is not on the forehead.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "always"?
If we say: always on his forehead,
can you find such a thing?!

phrases.aramaic: מִי לָא בָּעֵי מֵיעַל לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא,
phrases.english: Doesn't he need to go into the bathroom,
and doesn't he need to sleep?!
Rather: it always brings acceptance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 9 by rejecting the only other possible reading of 'תמיד.'
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's reading that 'תמיד' refers to constant acceptance
steps.raayaSupportSource: The real-life fact that the כהן גדול cannot wear the ציץ at all times (bathroom, sleep)

steps.title: What does רבי יהודה do with the word 'always'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה explains the word 'תמיד,' which is also written in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for רבי יהודה too, isn't 'always' written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי יהודה and challenges him. The same word 'תמיד' is in his פסוק too, so what does he learn from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 proved that 'תמיד' cannot mean 'always on the forehead.' So רבי יהודה cannot use the word to mean that, but he still has to give it some meaning. The challenge forces him to explain the word without agreeing with רבי שמעון's reading.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yehuda too,
isn't it written "always"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the proof from step 10 and uses it against רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's reading of the פסוק (step 8)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'תמיד' appears in the פסוק and cannot mean 'always on the forehead.' רבי יהודה must account for it, and the obvious meaning seems to support רבי שמעון.

steps.title: For רבי יהודה, 'always' means never losing awareness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers on behalf of רבי יהודה that 'תמיד' means the כהן גדול must never take his mind off the ציץ. This matches רבה בר רב הונא's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: That 'always' means he should not take his mind off it, like the teaching of רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יהודה. He uses 'תמיד' for a different lesson: the כהן גדול must stay constantly aware of the ציץ while wearing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'תמיד' describes the כהן גדול's mind, not where the ציץ is or what it does. That leaves רבי יהודה free to learn from 'on his forehead' that the ציץ works only when worn. The גמרא backs up this reading with a known teaching of רבה בר רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking one's mind off something / distraction (from 'שלא יסיח דעתו')
In line with the teaching of רבה בר רב הונא

phrases.english: That "always" means
that he should not take his mind off it,
in accordance with Rabba bar Rav Huna.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא תָּמִיד שֶׁלֹּא יַסִּיחַ דַּעְתּוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the word: it refers to the כהן גדול's awareness, not to the ציץ's power
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'תמיד' seemed to mean the ציץ always brings acceptance, which would support רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה, 'תמיד' means the כהן גדול must constantly be aware of the ציץ. So 'on his forehead' still limits when the ציץ works.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא: touch your תפילין every hour
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rules that a person must touch his תפילין regularly. He learns this through a קל וחומר from the ציץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה בר רב הונא said: a person must touch his תפילין every single hour, through a קל וחומר from the ציץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the teaching it just mentioned. It shows that 'not taking your mind off the ציץ' is a real הלכה that even carries over to תפילין. The explanation of the קל וחומר itself comes right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Touching the תפילין keeps a person aware that he is wearing them. The rule is learned from the ציץ, and that only works if 'תמיד' in the ציץ פסוק really means constant awareness. This confirms רבי יהודה's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: To touch / feel (to stay aware of)
תפילין worn on the head and arm
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case (or the reverse)
The gold plate worn on the כהן גדול's forehead

steps.whatToRemember: 'תמיד' in the ציץ פסוק is read two ways. רבי שמעון says it means the ציץ always brings acceptance, even off the head. רבי יהודה says it means the כהן גדול must always stay aware of the ציץ, and that is the source for regularly touching one's תפילין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical הלכה that a person wearing תפילין should touch them from time to time so he does not lose awareness of them.

phrases.english: As Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
A person is obligated to touch his tefillin
every single hour,
by an a fortiori argument from the tzitz:
phrases.notes: The details of the קל וחומר follow in the next part of the גמרא.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: חַיָּיב אָדָם לְמַשְׁמֵשׁ בִּתְפִילָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the teaching that step 12 referred to as support for רבי יהודה's reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person must touch his תפילין regularly to stay aware of them, learned by a קל וחומר from the ציץ.
